inboxSummary.title: Summarise yesterday's inbox
inboxSummary.body: Get a bulleted list of client decisions, supplier delays, and tasks—grouped by project.

phasedProposal.title: Draft a phased proposal
phasedProposal.body: Turn a brief into scope sections you can paste into your proposal template in minutes.

ffeSchedule.title: Refresh the FF&E schedule
ffeSchedule.body: Extract specs from URLs and flag long-lead items before they block install.

start.title: Start here
start.summary: Set guardrails before you automate—define what AI may draft, what humans must approve, and where project data lives.

sourceOfTruth.title: Name one source of truth
sourceOfTruth.body: Keep briefs, selections, and approvals in your project tool. AI outputs should reference that record, not a loose chat thread.

humanReview.title: Default to human review
humanReview.body: Use AI for first drafts: emails, task lists, spec summaries. A principal or PM approves anything client-facing.

logDecisions.title: Log decisions on the project
logDecisions.body: When AI suggests an alternate product or timeline shift, capture the decision in the project so procurement and finance stay aligned.

projectContext.label: Project context block
projectContext.text: You are assisting an interior design studio. Project: [name]. Phase: [concept/DD/procurement]. Budget band: [range]. Style: [keywords]. Only use facts from the notes below.

email.title: Email & client comms
email.summary: Turn inbox noise into routed actions—summaries, reply drafts, and approval reminders tied to the right project.

routeByProject.title: Route by project
routeByProject.body: Tag supplier threads separately from client threads. AI summaries should state which milestone or room they affect.

draftDontSend.title: Draft, don't send
draftDontSend.body: Generate empathetic, concise replies with clear next steps and dates. Designer edits tone before send.

surfaceBlockers.title: Surface blockers
surfaceBlockers.body: Ask AI to list open questions, missing selections, and overdue approvals from the last week of email.

clientUpdate.label: Client update email
clientUpdate.text: Draft a weekly client update for [project]. Tone: calm, professional. Include: completed this week, decisions needed, procurement status, next site date. Max 180 words.

chaseApproval.label: Chase approval
chaseApproval.text: Write a polite follow-up asking the client to approve [item] in the portal by [date]. Mention the impact on lead time if delayed.

procurement.title: Procurement & specs
procurement.summary: Use AI to compare alternates, sanity-check lead times, and keep FF&E schedules current without duplicate data entry.

specFromSupplier.title: Spec from supplier pages
specFromSupplier.body: Paste a product URL or cut sheet text; extract dimensions, finish, lead time, and compliance notes into your schedule format.

alternateWhenDelayed.title: Alternate when delayed
alternateWhenDelayed.body: When lead time slips, request two alternates with cost and aesthetic trade-offs in the same message to the client.

batchPoPrep.title: Batch PO prep
batchPoPrep.body: Group line items by vendor and flag minimum order values before generating purchase orders.

alternateProduct.label: Alternate product
alternateProduct.text: Original: [product]. Constraint: must ship within [weeks], similar scale and finish. Suggest 2 alternates with pros/cons for a client email.

tasks.title: Tasks & timelines
tasks.summary: Convert briefs and meeting notes into phased tasks with owners—then let AI keep the timeline honest as dates slip.

kickoffTaskMap.title: Kickoff → task map
kickoffTaskMap.body: Feed kickoff notes; output phases, tasks, owners, and due dates using your studio's standard phase names.

weeklyReplan.title: Weekly replan
weeklyReplan.body: Each Monday, list slipped tasks, dependencies at risk, and one recommended client communication.

kickoffTasks.label: Kickoff tasks
kickoffTasks.text: From these kickoff notes, create tasks for Concept, DD, Procurement, and Install. Each task: owner role, due date (+buffer), dependency. Notes: [paste].

proposals.title: Proposals & fees
proposals.summary: Accelerate fee proposals and scope letters while keeping commercial terms consistent with your templates.

scopeFromBrief.title: Scope from brief
scopeFromBrief.body: Turn a client brief into phased deliverables, exclusions, and assumptions before you price.

alignWithTemplate.title: Align with template
alignWithTemplate.body: Merge AI scope output into your Letter of Agreement and Proposal templates so legal language stays consistent.

scopeOutline.label: Scope outline
scopeOutline.text: Create a scope outline for a [residential/commercial] interior project. Include deliverables per phase, client responsibilities, and explicit exclusions. Brief: [paste].

governance.title: Governance & quality
governance.summary: Protect client trust—privacy, accuracy, and brand voice matter more than speed.

noConfidentialUploads.title: No confidential uploads
noConfidentialUploads.body: Do not paste client financials or personal data into public models. Use your studio's integrated AI where data stays in your workspace.

verifyNumbers.title: Verify numbers
verifyNumbers.body: AI must not invent dimensions, prices, or lead times. Confirm against supplier quotes and your library.

brandVoiceChecklist.title: Brand voice checklist
brandVoiceChecklist.body: Before send: warm but precise, no over-promising on dates, British English if that is your studio default.

tonePass.label: Tone pass
tonePass.text: Rewrite this email to match a premium interior design studio: concise, confident, no jargon. Keep facts identical: [paste].
